episodes.title: Pilot
episodes.summary: Walter White is a mild-mannered, underpaid high school chemistry teacher in Albuquerque, New Mexico, who also works part-time at a car wash. He lives with his pregnant wife Skyler and their teenage son, Walter White Jr., who has cerebral palsy. Skyler's sister Marie is married to Hank Schrader, a loud, confident DEA agent. Right after his 50th birthday, Walt collapses at the car wash and is diagnosed with inoperable lung cancer; even with treatment he may have only a couple of years left, and he keeps the news to himself. While riding along on one of Hank's DEA raids, Walt watches his former student Jesse Pinkman escape out a window as Jesse's partner Emilio Koyama is arrested, and he says nothing. Walt angrily quits the car wash, tracks Jesse down, and proposes a deal: Walt will cook methamphetamine and Jesse will sell it, so Walt can leave money for his family. Using Walt's savings and equipment taken from his school's chemistry lab, they buy an old RV and cook in the desert, and Walt's product is exceptionally pure. When Jesse brings a sample to the dealer Krazy-8, Emilio, now out on bail, recognizes Walt from the raid, and the two dealers force Jesse to lead them to the RV to kill both partners. Walt pretends to demonstrate his recipe and instead releases poisonous phosphine gas, trapping the dealers inside. Hearing sirens, Walt records a goodbye video for his family and waits in the road with a gun, but the sirens belong to fire trucks heading to a brush fire.

episodes.title: Cat's in the Bag...
episodes.summary: Walt and Jesse find that Emilio died from the gas but Krazy-8 survived, and they end up holding Krazy-8 prisoner in Jesse's basement, locked by the neck to a pole with a bicycle lock. They flip a coin to split the dirty work: Jesse must get rid of Emilio's body, and Walt must kill Krazy-8. Walt tells Jesse to dissolve the body in hydrofluoric acid inside a special plastic tub, but Jesse uses his upstairs bathtub instead; the acid eats through the tub and the floor, and the liquefied remains crash through the ceiling into the hallway below. Walt can't bring himself to kill Krazy-8 and instead keeps bringing him food and water. At home, Skyler notices Walt acting strangely and asks about a phone call with Jesse; Walt claims Jesse sells him marijuana, so Skyler visits Jesse and warns him she'll call her DEA brother-in-law if he sells to her husband again. In the desert, two kids find a gas mask Walt and Jesse accidentally left behind.

episodes.title: ...And the Bag's in the River
episodes.summary: Walt and Jesse scrape up the gruesome remains of Emilio's body. Walt agonizes over whether to kill Krazy-8, even writing out a list of reasons for and against. While bringing him a sandwich, Walt passes out on the basement stairs and the plate shatters. When he comes to, he admits to Krazy-8 that he has lung cancer, the first person he has told, and the two men talk at length and find things in common. Krazy-8 warns Walt not to trust a drug user like Jesse. Walt decides to let him go, but while piecing the broken plate back together, he realizes a sharp shard is missing and that Krazy-8 has hidden it as a weapon. When Walt goes back down, Krazy-8 lunges for him, and Walt strangles him to death with the bike lock. Meanwhile, Marie wrongly believes Walt Jr. is smoking marijuana, so Hank takes the boy to a seedy motel to scare him about where drug use can lead. Skyler catches Walt lying about working late at the car wash, since she already knows he quit weeks ago. That night Walt comes home and tells her they need to talk.

episodes.title: Cancer Man
episodes.summary: At a DEA briefing, Hank reports that Emilio and Krazy-8, who turns out to have been a DEA informant, have vanished, and that a new 99.1% pure meth is turning up in Albuquerque; he figures whoever is making it could become the city's next kingpin, with no idea it is Walt. With Skyler already aware of his diagnosis, Walt tells Walt Jr., Hank, and Marie about his cancer at a family barbecue, and Hank promises to always look out for the family. Skyler gets Walt in to see a top oncologist, Dr. Delcavoli, who says the cancer has reached his lymph nodes but may respond to chemotherapy. The treatment would cost about $90,000, and Walt hesitates to leave his family in debt if he dies anyway, which provokes a furious outburst from Walt Jr. Jesse, paranoid after smoking the product with his friends Skinny Pete and Combo, retreats to his parents' house and tries to connect with his overachieving younger brother, Jake. When a joint belonging to Jake turns up, Jesse takes the blame and is thrown out again. Jesse drops by Walt's house to talk business and hands over Walt's $4,000 share, but Walt angrily tells him to stay away. Pushed too far by an obnoxious stranger named Ken, Walt shorts out Ken's BMW battery with a squeegee at a gas station, setting the car on fire.

episodes.title: Gray Matter
episodes.summary: Walt and Skyler attend a lavish birthday party for Elliott Schwartz, Walt's old colleague from graduate school who is now the wealthy head of Gray Matter Technologies, and Walt reconnects with Elliott's wife Gretchen, with whom he shares a romantic past. Elliott offers Walt a well-paid job with good health insurance; Walt suspects Skyler told them about his cancer and refuses, unwilling to accept charity. Jesse, unable to land a legitimate job, tries to cook with his friend Badger, but the results fall far short of Walt's standard. Walt Jr. is caught trying to buy beer and calls Hank instead of his father, earning a lecture from Hank. Skyler stages a family intervention, with each person taking turns holding a 'talking pillow', to persuade Walt to start chemotherapy; Walt says he wants the right to choose for himself and doesn't want to spend his last months sick while leaving the family broke. The next morning he gives in and tells Skyler he'll accept Elliott and Gretchen's offer to pay for treatment, but when Gretchen calls, he turns down the money, falsely claiming his insurance covers it. Walt then shows up at Jesse's door, ready to cook again.

episodes.title: Crazy Handful of Nothin'
episodes.summary: Walt begins chemotherapy and tells Jesse how the partnership will work: Walt only cooks, and Jesse handles all the selling. During a cook, Jesse spots radiation marks on Walt's chest and realizes he has lung cancer. Hank traces the respirator found in the desert to the chemistry lab at Walt's school and arrests Hugo, the kindly school janitor, who has an old drug record and a little marijuana in his car, even though Walt knows Hugo didn't steal anything. When his hair starts falling out, Walt shaves his head. Their first batch nets only about $2,600, so Walt pushes to move larger amounts. Through Skinny Pete, Jesse approaches Tuco Salamanca, a volatile, violent distributor who has taken over Krazy-8's territory. When Jesse demands payment up front, Tuco steals the meth and beats Jesse so badly he lands in the hospital. Walt, now calling himself Heisenberg, walks into Tuco's headquarters with a bag of what looks like meth but is actually fulminated mercury, and throws a crystal to the floor, setting off an explosion that blows out the windows. Shaken, Tuco pays for the stolen meth and agrees to become their distributor.

episodes.title: A No-Rough-Stuff-Type Deal
episodes.summary: Walt has promised Tuco four pounds of meth, but he and Jesse can't buy enough cold medicine containing pseudoephedrine to make it. Walt decides to switch to a cooking method that uses methylamine, and the two break into a chemical warehouse at night, using homemade thermite to burn through the lock, and roll out a whole barrel of methylamine. Jesse is now living in the RV. Skyler hosts a baby shower where Marie gives her an expensive diamond tiara for the baby; when Skyler tries to return it, the store detains her because the tiara was stolen, and Marie flatly denies shoplifting it. At a junkyard, Walt and Jesse deliver the four pounds to Tuco and his men, No-Doze and Gonzo. When No-Doze speaks out of turn, Tuco erupts and savagely beats him in front of the horrified partners, then drives off, leaving Walt and Jesse to realize how dangerous their new distributor is.

episodes.title: Seven Thirty-Seven
episodes.summary: The season opens in black and white on a half-burned pink teddy bear floating in the Whites' swimming pool, with no explanation. At the junkyard, Tuco and his henchman Gonzo come back in a panic because No-Doze is dying from the beating; after he dies, Gonzo hides the body under a car. Terrified of Tuco, Walt calculates he needs $737,000 to secure his family's future and decides to kill Tuco with ricin, a poison he can make himself and that is hard to trace. The DEA finds No-Doze's body along with Gonzo, who bled to death in an accident at the junkyard, and launches a manhunt for Tuco; Hank also studies security footage from the methylamine warehouse break-in. When Hank, joking around, sends Walt a photo of Gonzo's body, Walt assumes Tuco killed his own man and will come for him and Jesse next. Skyler tells Hank about Marie's shoplifting and learns Marie is already in therapy for it. That night Walt sees headlights outside and finds Tuco holding Jesse at gunpoint; Tuco forces Walt into the car and drives off with both of them.

episodes.title: Grilled
episodes.summary: Tuco takes Walt and Jesse to a remote desert house where he looks after his uncle, Hector Salamanca, a former cartel boss who uses a wheelchair and, since a stroke, can only communicate by ringing a bell. Tuco explains that the DEA has rolled up his whole operation and, not knowing Gonzo died in an accident, is convinced Gonzo betrayed him. He announces he's taking Walt to Mexico to cook in a hidden jungle lab. Walt and Jesse try again and again to get Tuco to ingest the ricin, but Hector picks up on what they're doing and warns his nephew with his bell. Tuco attacks Jesse, but Jesse shoots him in the torso and escapes. Meanwhile, Skyler, frantic about Walt's disappearance, enlists Hank's help; Marie reveals that Walt has a second cell phone, and Skyler mentions the young man, Jesse, who has been selling Walt marijuana. Hank visits Jesse's mother, then tracks Jesse's car to Tuco's hideout, where he ends up in a shootout with Tuco and kills him. Walt and Jesse, watching from a distance, bury the gun and flee on foot into the desert.

episodes.title: Bit by a Dead Bee
episodes.summary: To explain where he has been, Walt strips naked in a supermarket and wanders the aisles as if confused, landing in the hospital, where he claims to remember nothing; doctors consider it a fugue state possibly linked to his cancer. Walt tells a hospital psychiatrist, in confidence, that he ran off simply to be alone and faked the episode to hide that from his family, and he is released. Jesse, now wanted for questioning, gets home and, with Badger's help, loads all of his lab equipment into the RV and has it towed away. He then sets up an alibi by holing up in a motel with a prostitute, claiming they spent the whole weekend together, and lets the DEA find him there. Hank brings Hector in to identify Jesse, but Hector refuses to cooperate. With nothing to hold him on, the DEA releases Jesse but keeps his money. Walt tells Jesse that nothing has changed and they will keep cooking.

episodes.title: Down
episodes.summary: With the disappearance behind them, Jesse is broke because the DEA took his money, and Walt can't leave the house without Skyler wondering where he is going. Jesse's parents, who own the house he lives in, evict him after Hank's visit to the family. Now homeless and with his motorbike stolen, Jesse sneaks into the lot where the RV is stored to sleep in it, and when the owner catches him, he drives the RV straight through the locked gate. Walt tries to reconnect with Walt Jr. by giving him a driving lesson. Skyler, unconvinced by Walt's denial that he has a second cell phone, starts leaving the house for long stretches without telling him where she goes, and Walt's frustration grows as he keeps denying everything. Finally Jesse shows up at Walt's house, and after an angry confrontation, Walt agrees to give him half of their remaining money.

episodes.title: Breakage
episodes.summary: Walt's chemotherapy is working, but his medical bills, including the cost of his fugue-state hospital stay, keep piling up. Jesse gets back on his feet, paying off his debts and renting a duplex apartment, where he is drawn to his next-door neighbor and landlord, Jane Margolis. Back in business, Jesse persuades Walt they should handle distribution themselves now that Tuco is gone, and recruits his friends Badger, Skinny Pete, and Combo as street dealers. Hank, newly promoted to a tri-state task force, is quietly suffering panic attacks after the Tuco shootout. The DEA keeps hearing the name Heisenberg but can't tell whether he's a real person or just a street legend. Skyler and Marie make peace over the tiara. When a pair of meth addicts rob Skinny Pete, Walt tells Jesse that if he doesn't respond, everyone will see them as easy targets.

episodes.title: Peekaboo
episodes.summary: Walt goes back to teaching. Gretchen Schwartz drops by the White house, where Skyler thanks her for paying Walt's medical bills, something Gretchen and Elliott have never done. Gretchen keeps the lie going in front of Skyler but confronts Walt privately; he lashes out, bitterly accusing her and Elliott of getting rich on work he helped create while he was left with nothing. Gretchen then tells Skyler they can no longer help with the bills, and Walt covers with a fresh lie. Meanwhile, Jesse goes after the addicts who robbed Skinny Pete, a man called Spooge and his girlfriend. At their filthy house he finds only their neglected little boy, whom he feeds and watches TV with while waiting. The couple returns with a stolen ATM they're trying to crack open, and they get the better of Jesse. When Spooge keeps insulting his girlfriend, she tips the ATM onto his head, killing him. Jesse takes back the drugs and cash, calls 911, leaves the boy safely on the porch, and slips away.

episodes.title: Negro y Azul
episodes.summary: The episode opens with a music video of a Mexican narcocorrido, a drug ballad about the legend of Heisenberg and his blue meth. Shaken by what happened at Spooge's house, Jesse hides at home and stops supplying his dealers, so Walt makes the deliveries himself. Walt learns the street now believes Jesse killed Spooge, and the fearsome reputation has customers paying up without trouble, so he decides it's time to expand into new territory. Skyler, looking for work, is rehired as a bookkeeper by her former boss, Ted Beneke. Jesse and Jane grow closer. Hank, now on the task force in El Paso, feels out of place among the other agents. When the team finds the severed head of a cartel informant called Tortuga mounted on a tortoise, Hank gets sick and walks away while the others mock him; then a bomb hidden on the tortoise explodes, killing and wounding several agents while Hank is unhurt.

episodes.title: Better Call Saul
episodes.summary: Hank returns to Albuquerque suffering from post-traumatic stress after the El Paso bombing; Walt tries to encourage him by describing how his cancer diagnosis made him stop living in fear, though Hank still has panic attacks. Jesse and Jane start sleeping together, and he learns she is a recovering addict. Badger is arrested in a police sting, and Walt and Jesse fear he will give up Heisenberg to cut a deal. They hire Saul Goodman, a flashy, shady criminal lawyer known for his cheesy TV ads. When Saul suggests Badger should trade Heisenberg for leniency, Walt and Jesse, wearing masks, drag him to the desert and threaten him. Saul instead proposes a workaround: an ex-convict nicknamed Jimmy In-'N-Out, who gets paid to serve time for other people, will pose as Heisenberg in a staged buy set up through Badger. The DEA arrests the decoy and Badger gets off lightly, though Hank isn't fully convinced. Saul then has a private investigator track Walt down at school and offers to be his full-time lawyer and adviser in exchange for a cut of the profits.

episodes.title: 4 Days Out
episodes.summary: Coughing up blood, Walt is convinced his cancer is getting worse, and when Saul runs the numbers on what Walt has actually saved after laundering costs, Walt realizes there is far too little for his family. Telling Skyler he is visiting his mother, Walt takes Jesse into the remote desert for a marathon cook to produce as much meth as possible. Jesse accidentally leaves the keys in the ignition, draining the RV's battery, and the two are stranded for days, running out of water and food. As hope fades, Walt uses chemistry to build a crude battery out of materials scavenged from the RV, generating enough power to jump-start the engine. Back in Albuquerque, Walt and Skyler learn his tumor has shrunk dramatically and the cancer is in remission. The family is thrilled, but Walt, alone in a hospital restroom, angrily punches a paper-towel dispenser.

episodes.title: Over
episodes.summary: With his cancer in remission, Walt tells Jesse he is getting out of the drug business now that he no longer needs money for treatment. Skyler throws a party to celebrate and thank their friends. Walt, drinking heavily, keeps pouring tequila for Walt Jr. until the boy throws up into the pool, and he turns on Hank when Hank steps in; afterward Walt tries to make amends. Restless, Walt becomes fixated on repairing the house, tearing out rotting floorboards and replacing the water heater. At work, Skyler breaks down and confides in Ted about Walt's illness. Jane's father, Donald, drops in unexpectedly, and Jane introduces Jesse only as her tenant, which hurts him; she later apologizes and they reconcile. At a hardware store, Walt spots two amateurs loading up on meth-making supplies and coldly warns them to stay out of his territory.

episodes.title: Mandala
episodes.summary: Combo, one of Jesse's dealers, is shot dead on a street corner by a young boy working for a rival gang, and a shaken Skinny Pete quits. With no distribution network left, Saul sets up a meeting with a major meth distributor at a Los Pollos Hermanos fast-food restaurant. The distributor turns out to be Gus Fring, the courteous owner of the chain, who at first seems to be just another employee. Put off when Jesse arrives late and high, Gus initially refuses to deal; after Walt comes back alone, Gus agrees to buy from him but warns him never to trust a drug addict. Grieving Combo, Jesse tells Jane what he really does for a living. Jane relapses and introduces Jesse to heroin, and the two start using together. At work, Skyler discovers Ted has been falsifying the company's books to avoid taxes but decides not to report him. Gus offers Walt a large payment if he can deliver his entire 38-pound inventory within an hour, but Jesse is passed out on heroin and the meth is at his place. At that exact moment, Skyler calls: she is in labor.

episodes.title: Phoenix
episodes.summary: Walt delivers the meth to Gus on time and collects $1.2 million, but misses the birth of his daughter, Holly. He refuses to hand Jesse his share until Jesse gets clean. Jane's father, Donald, discovers she and Jesse are using and gives her one day before she goes to rehab. To help cover Walt's upcoming surgery, Walt Jr. launches a website, SaveWalterWhite.com, asking for donations, and Saul turns it into a way to launder Walt's money as fake online gifts. Jane figures out how much Jesse is owed and blackmails Walt into paying, threatening to expose him. Later, at a bar, Walt has a heartfelt conversation about family with a stranger who is worried about his own daughter; the man is Donald, though neither realizes the connection. Walt then goes to Jesse's apartment to reconcile and finds Jesse and Jane passed out after a heroin binge. As Walt shakes Jesse, Jane rolls onto her back, vomits, and begins to choke. Walt moves to help, then stops, and watches her die.

episodes.title: ABQ
episodes.summary: Jesse wakes to find Jane dead beside him and calls Walt in a panic. Walt calls Saul, who sends Mike, a calm, methodical fixer, to clean up the scene and coach Jesse so nothing points to him. Consumed by guilt, Jesse disappears; Walt finds him in a crack house and puts him into rehab. Laundered money floods into Walt Jr.'s donation website, drawing local news coverage that leaves Walt ashamed. As he goes under anesthesia for his lung surgery, Walt mentions his second cell phone. Skyler starts digging and uncovers his lies, including that Gretchen and Elliott never paid for his treatment and that he never visited his mother, and she leaves him, taking the children. Donald, an air traffic controller, goes back to work devastated by Jane's death and makes an error that causes an airliner and a small plane to collide over Albuquerque. Wreckage and human remains rain down across the city, including onto the Whites' house, where the charred pink teddy bear lands in their pool.

episodes.title: No Más
episodes.summary: In the opening, two silent twin brothers in sharp suits crawl to a shrine of Santa Muerte in Mexico and leave behind a drawing of Heisenberg. Albuquerque is reeling from the midair collision, and Walt, who has worked out that Jane's grieving father Donald caused it, starts burning bundles of his drug money in the backyard grill before changing his mind and tossing the burning cash into the pool. Skyler has moved out with Walt Jr. and baby Holly so Walt can pack and leave; Hank helps him move into an apartment, laughing off Walt's admission that one bag holds $500,000. At a school assembly about the crash, Walt gives an awkward speech pointing out that far deadlier air disasters have happened. After meeting with a divorce lawyer, Skyler hands Walt divorce papers and accuses him of dealing drugs; Walt admits he cooks methamphetamine. Horrified, she promises to keep his secret if he grants her a divorce and full custody. In rehab, Jesse decides to stop hating himself and accept that he is the bad guy. Walt tells Gus he is quitting and turns down an offer of $3 million for three months of work. Meanwhile, the twins cross into the U.S. hidden in a truck with other migrants; when a fellow passenger spots a sign of their cartel ties, they murder everyone aboard and blow up the truck.

episodes.title: Caballo sin Nombre
episodes.summary: Pulled over for a cracked windshield, Walt mouths off to the officer and lands in the back of a police car, but Hank gets the matter dropped. Skyler, back at work for Ted, refuses to let Walt come home, which confuses and angers Walt Jr. Saul pushes Walt to keep cooking for Gus; when Walt refuses, Saul has his associate Mike secretly watch and bug the White house. Jesse, out of rehab, finds his parents have renovated his old house and put it up for sale. He has Saul buy it from them at a lowball price by threatening to reveal that it once held a meth lab, which would tie up any sale in legal trouble. The twin brothers are revealed to be Leonel and Marco Salamanca, Tuco's cousins. They visit their uncle Hector at his nursing home, and he gives them Walt's name. Walt breaks back into his own house and settles in. While he showers, the cousins wait inside with an axe, but they receive a one-word text message and leave without harming him.

episodes.title: I.F.T.
episodes.summary: Walt moves back into the house and tells Skyler he isn't leaving. Walt Jr. is thrilled, but Skyler calls the police, who can't remove Walt without a court order, and she stops short of telling them what he does. Skyler admits to her divorce lawyer that Walt makes meth; the lawyer urges her to go to the police, but Skyler can't bear for Walt Jr. to learn the truth about his father. Without Walt knowing, Gus meets with Tuco's cousins and Hector and makes clear that Walt is not to be touched for now. Jesse, still grieving Jane, settles back into his old house. Hank, learning he is being sent back to El Paso, picks a fight with two men in a bar and beats them badly. Walt pleads with Skyler that everything he did was for the family and begs her to accept the money. Instead, Skyler goes to work and sleeps with Ted, then calmly tells Walt that night that she has been unfaithful.

episodes.title: Green Light
episodes.summary: Jesse trades a gas station cashier some meth for a tank of gas. Walt barges into Beneke Fabricators to confront Ted, and Mike hustles him out before the police arrive. When Walt learns Saul bugged his house, he fires Saul on the spot, losing his help laundering money. Walt makes a clumsy pass at the school principal, Carmen Molina, and is put on indefinite leave. On his way out, he is met by Jesse, who has cooked his own batch using Walt's recipe; Walt dismisses it as inferior, so Jesse sells it to Gus through Saul and Mike. Gus reluctantly buys it, betting that Walt's pride and need for money will bring him back; Jesse receives only half the payment, and the other half is delivered to Walt. Hank turns down his transfer to El Paso to chase a new lead in the Heisenberg case: security footage of Jesse's RV at that gas station.

episodes.title: Más
episodes.summary: Walt figures out that Gus sent him half of Jesse's payment to lure him back, and he still says no. Gus makes a final pitch by showing Walt a state-of-the-art superlab hidden beneath an industrial laundry. Walt is amazed but declines, saying the business has already cost him his family; Gus replies that a man provides for his family even when he isn't appreciated for it. Hank keeps chasing the RV and argues with Marie, who confides her worries to Skyler. That makes Skyler question her affair with Ted and reconsider Walt's money, but when she comes home she finds Walt has signed the divorce papers and moved out, taking his belongings and his money. At Saul's office, Walt gives Jesse his share of the money and announces he has decided to cook for Gus after all, leaving Jesse furious and Saul delighted. Hank discovers the RV belonged to the mother of Combo, Jesse's dead friend.

episodes.title: Sunset
episodes.summary: Walt moves into a condo and starts work in the superlab, where he quickly warms to his new assistant, Gale, a highly trained chemist who shares his passion for chemistry and brews coffee with lab equipment. Jesse starts dealing again with Badger and Skinny Pete. Walt Jr. demands answers about his parents' split. Hank stakes out Jesse, convinced he still has the RV. Realizing Hank has tied Jesse to the RV, Walt arranges to have it destroyed at Old Joe's junkyard. Jesse arrives angry, Hank tails him there, and the partners end up trapped inside the RV while Hank stands outside, unaware Walt is in there. Saul's secretary calls Hank pretending Marie has been badly hurt in a car accident, and Hank races off; he only realizes he was tricked when he reaches the hospital. Walt and Jesse watch the RV get crushed. Gus, knowing Tuco's cousins won't wait much longer to kill Walt, steers their vengeance toward Hank, the DEA agent who actually shot Tuco.

episodes.title: One Minute
episodes.summary: Furious about the fake hospital call, Hank storms Jesse's house and beats him badly. From his hospital bed, Jesse vows to sue Hank and ruin his career, and threatens to turn Walt in if Walt or Saul get in his way. Skyler pushes Walt to get Jesse to drop the charges. Walt deliberately sours things with Gale and, over Gus' objections, offers Jesse a partnership in the superlab; Jesse refuses at first but then accepts. Hank breaks down to Marie, saying he hasn't been the same since killing Tuco and that he is finished as a cop; he admits the assault to his bosses and is suspended without pay and stripped of his gun. In a parking lot, Hank gets an anonymous call warning that two men are coming to kill him in one minute. Tuco's cousins shoot him several times, but Hank pins Leonel between two cars by ramming him in reverse, then kills Marco with a shot to the head.

episodes.title: I See You
episodes.summary: Jesse leaves the hospital just as Hank is wheeled in in critical condition. Hank's family gathers in the waiting room: Marie lashes out at Hank's boss for taking his gun and blames Walt for pointing Hank toward Jesse. The attack on a DEA agent sets off a crackdown in Mexico, and cartel boss Juan Bolsa calls Gus wanting to know who authorized the hit. Walt fires Gale and brings in Jesse as his partner, but while Walt is stuck at the hospital, Jesse struggles alone in the lab to hit their quota. Walt sees the surviving cousin, Leonel, recovering in the same hospital and realizes he himself may have been the real target. Gus shows up at the hospital, and Walt realizes Gus has known all along that Hank is his brother-in-law. Shortly after Gus leaves, Leonel goes into cardiac arrest and dies, and Mike quietly drops a used syringe into a sharps container on his way out. In Mexico, Juan Bolsa is gunned down in his home while on the phone with Gus.

episodes.title: Kafkaesque
episodes.summary: The superlab is running smoothly at about 200 pounds of meth a week, and Jesse secretly skims some of the extra to sell on the side with Badger and Skinny Pete. Hank survives but faces a long recovery, and Marie learns their insurance won't cover the quality of physical therapy he needs to walk again. Skyler, believing Walt is at least indirectly responsible for the shooting, offers to pay for Hank's treatment and invents a cover story that Walt won a fortune gambling. Marie is stunned but accepts. Gomez shows Hank that blue meth is now turning up in several states, a sign that Heisenberg is still active. When Hank mentions the anonymous warning call, Walt realizes the cousins were really after him and suspects Gus redirected them onto Hank. Walt thanks Gus, who promises him protection and raises the idea of extending their arrangement to a full year.

episodes.title: Fly
episodes.summary: Plagued by insomnia and dread about where his life is heading, Walt also notices the lab's output falling slightly short of his calculations, unaware that Jesse has been skimming. When a single housefly gets into the lab, Walt becomes obsessed with killing it to prevent contamination and halts production. Jesse thinks it is absurd at first but helps, and after learning Walt hasn't slept in days, secretly slips sleeping pills into his coffee. As the pills take hold, Walt rambles about a moment when it would have been perfect to die and comes close to confessing what happened the night Jane died, even mentioning that he met her father in a bar that night, before stopping himself. While Walt sleeps, Jesse finishes the batch alone. The next morning, Walt quietly warns Jesse that the lab may have hidden cameras and that he won't be able to protect him if Gus finds out about the missing meth.

episodes.title: Abiquiú
episodes.summary: A flashback shows Jesse and Jane visiting the Georgia O'Keeffe Museum. In the present, Hank's hospital bills start arriving, and Skyler, worried the payments could be traced to drug money, insists on managing Walt's finances. Walt introduces her to Saul, whose laundering plan she finds unconvincing, and she proposes a more believable business: the car wash where Walt used to work. Hank refuses to leave the hospital until he can walk, frustrating Marie. Gus invites Walt to dinner at his home and offers him some guidance. Looking to sell the meth he has been skimming, Jesse targets Andrea, a woman from his recovery group; they start dating, but he decides not to sell to her when he meets her young son, Brock. Jesse then learns that Andrea's 11-year-old brother, Tomás, was the boy who shot Combo, and he confirms Tomás now works for dealers selling blue meth, which means they are part of Gus' operation.

episodes.title: Half Measures
episodes.summary: Jesse plans revenge on the two dealers who used Tomás to kill Combo and asks Walt for help. Walt refuses but, afraid Jesse will get himself killed, tries to defuse the situation, and Gus calls a meeting with Jesse and the dealers. Gus orders the dealers to stop using children, and Jesse reluctantly agrees to keep the peace. Mike tells Walt a story from his days as a police officer about an abusive husband he let off with a beating and a warning rather than killing, who went on to murder his wife, explaining why he no longer takes half measures. Soon after the meeting, the dealers kill Tomás. Hearing about the boy's death on the news, Walt rushes out, guessing Jesse is about to do something reckless. As Jesse walks up to the dealers with a gun and they draw theirs, Walt speeds in and runs both men down with his car, then picks up a gun and shoots the survivor in the head. He tells a stunned Jesse to run. Meanwhile, Marie finally coaxes a reluctant Hank into leaving the hospital.

episodes.title: Full Measure
episodes.summary: Gus meets Walt in the desert after the dealers' deaths. Walt claims Jesse has fled the state, and Gus, his patience clearly worn thin, lets Walt go back to work but brings back Gale as his assistant. Watching Gus with Gale, Walt realizes Gus plans to have Gale learn his formula and then have Walt killed, since Gale is the only other chemist who could replace him. Walt concludes that Gale must die: if Walt is the only cook left, Gus will have to keep him, and by extension Jesse, alive. Before Walt can act, Gus' henchman Victor picks him up and takes him to the laundry, where Mike is waiting to kill him. Under the pretense of luring Jesse in, Walt phones him and tells him to get to Gale's apartment and kill him immediately. Victor races to Gale's home, but Jesse gets there first. In tears, Jesse points his gun at Gale as Gale pleads with him, and fires.

episodes.title: Box Cutter
episodes.summary: Walt and Jesse are held in the superlab by Mike and Victor while they wait for Gus to react to Gale's murder. Victor, trying to prove the partners are replaceable, starts cooking a batch himself using what he has seen of their process. Skyler can't reach Walt and fears the worst, and a paranoid Saul hires a bodyguard. Hank, recovering at home, takes his frustration out on Marie and becomes absorbed in collecting minerals. Gus finally arrives, silently changes into a lab suit, and slits Victor's throat with a box cutter in front of Walt, Jesse, and Mike, then changes back into his work clothes and tells the partners to get back to work. Afterward, Walt tells Jesse that killing Gale was necessary, but they both know Gus could kill them at any moment. Detectives comb through Gale Boetticher's apartment without realizing what his lab notebook contains.

episodes.title: Thirty-Eight Snub
episodes.summary: Convinced Gus will kill him first, Walt buys an untraceable .38 snub-nosed revolver from an illegal arms dealer named Lawson and starts carrying it, planning to shoot Gus. Mike and Gus' new enforcer, Tyrus, make it clear Walt will never get near Gus again. Jesse, trying to drown out his guilt over Gale, buys a massive sound system and turns his house into a nonstop party with Badger and Skinny Pete. Andrea visits, worried about him, and Jesse hands her a thick stack of cash for Brock's future. At home, Marie struggles to cope with Hank's sullen depression as he goes through physical therapy. Skyler pushes ahead with her plan to buy the car wash, but Walt's resentful former boss, Bogdan, refuses to sell. Believing Mike is in as much danger as he is, Walt tracks him to a bar and asks for help getting into a room with Gus so he can kill him. Mike answers by beating Walt to the floor and walking out.

episodes.title: Open House
episodes.summary: Walt is enraged to find that a surveillance camera has been installed in the lab. Skyler persuades Walt to go ahead with buying the car wash, and to pressure the owner, she has one of Saul's con men pose as an environmental inspector who threatens to shut the business down over contamination. Bogdan caves and sells for even less than Skyler first offered. Jesse keeps his house open for round-the-clock, drug-fueled parties and deliberately tosses piles of cash into the chaos. Feeling shut out by Hank, Marie relapses into shoplifting, inventing fake identities to tour houses for sale and pocket small items. She is caught and arrested, and Hank calls in a favor with a police detective to get her released without charges. In return, the detective asks Hank to help with the Gale Boetticher murder and gives him a copy of Gale's lab notebook.

episodes.title: Bullet Points
episodes.summary: In the opening, Mike rides hidden in the refrigerated cargo hold of a Los Pollos Hermanos truck when cartel gunmen force it off the road and kill the driver; when they open the doors, Mike shoots them dead, though a bullet nicks his ear. Walt and Skyler rehearse, then deliver at a family dinner, a staged confession that Walt won big by counting cards, explaining how they paid for Hank's care and bought the car wash. Snooping in Hank's bedroom, Walt finds the case file on Gale's murder. Hank tells Walt he believes Gale was the cook behind the blue meth, Heisenberg himself, shows him a video of Gale singing karaoke, and asks him to read from Gale's lab notebook, which contains a Walt Whitman poem and a dedication to 'W.W.' When Hank teases that the initials match Walt's, Walt plays along, then says they must refer to the poet. Walt is disgusted to find Jesse's house turned into a drug den and learns Jesse left a shell casing behind when he shot Gale; Walt also turns down Saul's suggestion that he go into hiding. Thieves make off with more than $70,000 of Jesse's money, and though Mike quickly recovers it, Jesse's indifference convinces Mike to tell Gus that Jesse has become a problem. The episode ends with Mike driving a silent Jesse to an unknown destination.

episodes.title: Shotgun
episodes.summary: Mike assures a worried Walt that Jesse is safe, and spends the day taking Jesse along on cash pickups across New Mexico. At the last stop, a man with a shotgun tries to rob them, and Jesse scares him off and saves the money; afterward Gus and Mike are seen discussing how they staged the robbery to build up Jesse's confidence and loyalty. Walt and Skyler finalize the car wash purchase, and Skyler asks Walt to move back into the house. At a family dinner, Hank says he has closed the book on Gale, convinced Gale was Heisenberg and a genius. A tipsy Walt can't stand hearing Gale praised and argues that Gale was probably just copying someone else's work, implying the real genius is still out there. Re-energized, Hank goes back through Gale's belongings and finds a Los Pollos Hermanos napkin.

episodes.title: Cornered
episodes.summary: Rattled by Walt's behavior at dinner, Skyler fears he is in danger and urges him to go to the police. Walt explodes, insisting that he is not the one in danger but the one others should fear, and a shaken Skyler drives off with Holly. Walt tells Jesse that Gus is trying to drive a wedge between them and correctly guesses that the robbery Jesse stopped was staged. Jesse is again pulled out of the lab to work with Mike. Walt pays three laundry workers to clean the lab, and when Gus finds out, he has them deported. Gus praises Jesse's work and tells him he sees potential in him, deepening Jesse's loyalty. Walt gives in to Walt Jr.'s pleas for a car and buys him a flashy Dodge Challenger. Skyler demands he return it because it undermines their gambling cover story, and warns that the family now needs protection from Walt himself.

episodes.title: Problem Dog
episodes.summary: Forced to return the Challenger, Walt takes it to an empty parking lot, does reckless doughnuts, crashes it, and sets it on fire, leaving Saul to clean up the mess. Skyler realizes how much money Walt is making and worries she can't launder it all through the car wash. Walt persuades Jesse, who now has close access to Gus, to poison him, and makes ricin in the lab, which Jesse hides inside a cigarette. At a meeting where cartel representatives deliver an ultimatum that Gus rejects, Jesse has a chance to slip Gus the poison but doesn't take it. Jesse returns to his recovery group and, after telling a thinly veiled story about putting down a dog, admits he has been using the group to find customers; the group leader throws him out. Hank takes Walt Jr. to Los Pollos Hermanos and secretly collects Gus' fingerprints from a drink cup. He then presents his theory to Gomez and his boss: Gus' prints match prints found in Gale's apartment, and Hank believes Gus runs a large meth operation.

episodes.title: Hermanos
episodes.summary: A flashback shows Gus visiting Hector at the nursing home to tell him his nephews are dead after their attempt on Hank. In the present, Gus calmly answers questions from Hank, the DEA, and Albuquerque police, explaining that Gale was a recipient of a chemistry scholarship he funds and had recently had him over to ask for money, which is why his fingerprints were in Gale's apartment. The investigators are satisfied, but Hank isn't. Hank recruits Walt to drive him around and plant a GPS tracker on Gus' car. Walt warns Gus about the tracker, and Gus calmly tells him to plant it anyway. Suspecting Jesse's loyalty is shifting, Walt presses him to poison Gus as soon as possible. A longer flashback to 1989 shows Gus and his partner Max, a talented chemist, pitching high-quality meth to cartel boss Don Eladio; at Eladio's order, Hector shoots Max dead while Gus is forced to watch. In the present, Gus hints to Hector that his revenge is coming.

episodes.title: Bug
episodes.summary: Ted tells Skyler the IRS is auditing him for fraud. Afraid she will be implicated as his former bookkeeper, Skyler attends the audit and plays a ditzy, unqualified employee, which keeps the auditors from digging deeper, but Ted still owes more than $600,000 in back taxes and penalties. Skyler checks on the cash she has been hiding in the crawl space under the house. With the tracker data from Gus' car turning up nothing, Hank sets his sights on Gus' distribution center, and Jesse has to help clear all the product out in time. A cartel sniper opens fire on the facility, pinning down Gus' workers until Gus walks out alone into the open; Mike explains to Jesse that the cartel won't kill Gus because it needs his distribution network. Gus finally agrees to the cartel's terms and tells Jesse he will be sent to Mexico to teach the cartel's chemists to make the blue meth. Walt confronts Jesse about not poisoning Gus, and the argument turns into a brutal fistfight in Walt's condo.

episodes.title: Salud
episodes.summary: Skyler has Saul invent an inheritance from a distant relative so she can secretly give Ted about $620,000 to pay off the IRS. Instead, Ted leases a Mercedes and tries to restart his business, so Skyler admits the money came from her. Battered from his fight with Jesse, Walt misses Walt Jr.'s birthday party. Walt Jr. visits his father's condo, finds him bloodied, and hears Walt blame it on gambling. As Walt drifts off on painkillers, he calls his son Jesse. The next morning Walt apologizes and says he doesn't want to be remembered that way, but Walt Jr. says he would rather remember this honest version of his father than the man he has been for the past year. In Mexico, Jesse impresses the cartel's skeptical chemists with a 96% pure batch, but is told he now belongs to the cartel. At Don Eladio's estate, Gus brings a bottle of tequila to celebrate their alliance; having taken pills beforehand, he drinks it to put Eladio at ease, then forces himself to vomit as Eladio and his top men die from the poison. A cartel gunman shoots Mike, Jesse kills the shooter, and Jesse drives the wounded Gus and Mike to safety.

episodes.title: Crawl Space
episodes.summary: Gus survives the poisoning with the help of a doctor waiting nearby, while Mike must stay behind in Mexico to recover from his wound. Gus tells Jesse he can now run the lab on his own, and Jesse asks only that Walt not be killed. Gus visits Hector at the nursing home to taunt him that Don Eladio and the rest of the cartel's leaders are dead. Ted still won't pay the IRS, so Skyler sends Saul's men, Huell and Kuby, to scare him into signing a check; Ted signs, then tries to run, trips, and slams his head into a counter. Walt deliberately crashes the car he is driving to stop Hank from checking out the industrial laundry, but Hank remains undeterred. Walt learns Jesse has been cooking without him and begs him to stop, but Jesse won't. Gus has Walt hooded and taken to the desert, fires him, and warns that he will deal with Hank himself and kill Walt's entire family if Walt interferes. Walt has Saul call in an anonymous tip that Hank is in danger, then rushes home to pay a contact of Saul's who can give the family new identities, only to find most of the money in the crawl space gone because Skyler gave it to Ted. Walt breaks down, laughing hysterically on the crawl space floor, as Marie calls to say the DEA has received a threat against Hank and is putting him under protection.

episodes.title: End Times
episodes.summary: After the anonymous tip, the DEA moves Skyler, Walt Jr., and Holly into Hank and Marie's house for protection, while Walt refuses to go. At Hank's urging, Gomez searches the industrial laundry but finds nothing. Gus tells Jesse that Walt is to blame for the police attention and must be killed, but Jesse still refuses to cook if Walt dies. Andrea calls Jesse to the hospital because Brock is critically ill with mysterious flu-like symptoms. Jesse discovers the ricin cigarette he has been carrying is missing and becomes convinced Brock was poisoned. He storms Walt's house and holds him at gunpoint, accusing him of poisoning the boy; Walt, desperate, convinces Jesse that Gus must be behind it, and the two agree that Gus has to die. Gus comes to the hospital to demand Jesse return to work, but Jesse won't leave Brock. Walt builds a homemade bomb and plants it under Gus' car in the hospital parking garage, but Gus senses something is wrong and walks away from the car.

episodes.title: Face Off
episodes.summary: Detectives question Jesse about Brock's suspected poisoning until Saul intervenes. Walt, Jesse, and Saul realize Gus' weak spot is his habit of visiting Hector at the Casa Tranquila nursing home. Walt visits Hector, his old enemy, who agrees to help. Gus' men pull Jesse from the hospital and force him to cook in the superlab. Following Walt's plan, Hector asks to meet with the DEA, which leads Gus to believe Hector is becoming an informant. Gus goes to Hector's room to kill him personally and taunts him first; Hector rings his bell, setting off a bomb Walt built into his wheelchair, which kills Gus, his henchman Tyrus, and Hector himself. Walt rescues Jesse from the lab, and they set it on fire. At the hospital, Jesse tells Walt that Brock is recovering and was poisoned not by ricin but by berries from a lily of the valley plant; they agree Gus had to die anyway. Skyler sees the news and calls, and Walt tells her that he has won. The final shot shows a potted lily of the valley plant in Walt's backyard, revealing that Walt himself poisoned Brock.

episodes.title: Live Free or Die
episodes.summary: A flash-forward opens the season: on his 52nd birthday, a disheveled Walt, using a false name and passing himself off as being from New Hampshire, eats breakfast alone at an Albuquerque Denny's and buys an M60 machine gun from the arms dealer Lawson, who leaves it in the trunk of a car. In the present, Walt gets rid of the evidence linking him to Gus' death and Brock's poisoning, and Skyler tells him she is now afraid of him. Walt realizes the lab's security cameras could incriminate them, and the footage may be on Gus' laptop, now in police evidence. Mike returns from Mexico ready to kill Walt over Gus' death, but agrees the laptop has to be dealt with first. At Jesse's suggestion, they rig a truck with a huge electromagnet from Old Joe's junkyard and use it to wipe the laptop through the wall of the police evidence room, abandoning the truck as they escape. Skyler visits Ted, who is in a halo brace after his fall and too frightened to tell anyone what happened. Saul reveals that, on Walt's instructions, his bodyguard Huell pickpocketed Jesse's ricin cigarette; disturbed that Walt poisoned a child, Saul tries to cut ties, but Walt tells him they are done only when Walt says so. That night Walt embraces Skyler and tells her he forgives her for giving Ted the money.

episodes.title: Madrigal
episodes.summary: In Germany, Peter Schuler, an executive at Madrigal Electromotive, the conglomerate that owns Los Pollos Hermanos, kills himself with a defibrillator as police arrive to question him about Gus. Back in Albuquerque, Jesse panics over the missing ricin cigarette; Walt hides the real ricin vial behind an electrical outlet cover at home, makes a fake cigarette, and plants it in Jesse's Roomba while helping him search. When Jesse 'finds' it, he breaks down, ashamed he ever suspected Walt of poisoning Brock. Walt and Jesse offer Mike Ehrmantraut a three-way partnership in a new meth operation, but Mike refuses, calling Walt a time bomb. Hank's boss, George Merkert, is pushed out of his job for missing the signs about his friend Gus. Hank and Gomez question Mike, who learns the DEA has seized the offshore accounts Gus set up for his men, including $2 million in his granddaughter's name. Lydia Rodarte-Quayle, a jittery Madrigal executive in Houston, wants Gus' former men silenced; when Mike refuses, she hires one of his own men, who kills Gus' methylamine supplier, Duane Chow, and lies in wait for Mike. Mike kills the hitman and nearly executes Lydia, but spares her in exchange for a supply of methylamine, then calls Walt to accept the partnership. Skyler, terrified of Walt, withdraws into silence.

episodes.title: Hazard Pay
episodes.summary: Walt moves back into the family home, to Skyler's dismay. Needing a new place to cook, Walt comes up with the idea of setting up inside houses being tented for fumigation by Vamonos Pest, an exterminator whose crew, Saul explains, secretly burglarizes the homes it treats. Walt subtly steers Jesse into breaking up with Andrea by pointing out the danger of her learning his secrets. At the car wash, Skyler has a breakdown in front of Marie; when Marie demands answers, Walt tells her about Skyler's affair with Ted and blames her collapse on guilt over Ted's accident. After the first successful cook, Walt is angered by how much of the profit goes to 'hazard pay' for Mike's men in prison, who are being paid to stay silent. Bitter that he is earning less than he did under Gus, Walt hints to Jesse that some members of their crew may need to be removed.

episodes.title: Fifty-One
episodes.summary: Walt celebrates his 51st birthday, a year after his diagnosis, and Jesse gives him a watch as a gift. With the DEA probing Madrigal, Lydia gives up one of her own warehouse employees to investigators, and Jesse takes over collecting methylamine with her; together they discover a GPS tracker on one of the barrels. Because it seems crudely placed, Mike suspects Lydia planted it herself to get out of the deal. Hank is promoted to Assistant Special Agent in Charge of the Albuquerque DEA office. Skyler sinks deeper into depression. At a small birthday dinner, while Walt talks about how lucky he feels, Skyler walks fully clothed into the swimming pool and lets herself sink until Walt pulls her out. Walt learns she has arranged for Hank and Marie to keep the kids. In a tense late-night conversation, Walt threatens to have her committed, and Skyler admits that all she can do is wait for his cancer to come back and kill him.

episodes.title: Dead Freight
episodes.summary: Pretending to break down in tears in Hank's new office, Walt plants listening devices there and learns that the tracker on the methylamine barrel was placed by a DEA team in Houston, clearing Lydia. With that supply now compromised, Lydia, desperate to stay alive, proposes stealing a huge load of methylamine from a freight train. The crew enlists Todd, a polite young Vamonos Pest employee, to help, and Jesse insists that no one must ever know about the heist. Walt Jr., angry about being sent to stay with Hank and Marie, comes home demanding to stay, but Walt sends him back. Skyler tells Walt she will keep laundering his money and keep his secrets as long as the children stay away. The heist works: they stop the train in the desert and pump out about a thousand gallons of methylamine, refilling the tank with water so the weight doesn't change. As they finish, a boy on a dirt bike rides up and sees them; after a tense pause, Todd draws a gun and shoots him dead, to Jesse's horror.

episodes.title: Buyout
episodes.summary: The crew disposes of the dead boy's body and his dirt bike. Shaken by the killing and under heavy DEA surveillance, Jesse and Mike decide to quit and sell their shares of the stolen methylamine to Declan, a rival distributor from Phoenix, for $5 million each, but Walt refuses to sell his share, which kills the deal. Walt invites Jesse over and confides that he once sold his stake in Gray Matter for $5,000, a company now worth billions, and that he won't settle for less again. A dinner with Skyler turns painfully awkward when she openly mentions her affair, and Walt later tells Jesse that Skyler is just waiting for him to die and the business is all he has left. Mike and Saul obtain a court order that stops the DEA from following Mike. Mike zip-ties Walt to a radiator to keep him from interfering, but Walt burns through the tie with an exposed electrical wire and hides the methylamine. When Mike threatens to kill him, Walt says he has a plan in which everyone wins.

episodes.title: Say My Name
episodes.summary: In the desert, Walt meets Declan and makes him say the name Heisenberg, acknowledging Walt as the cook behind the famous blue meth. Walt negotiates a new arrangement: Declan will distribute Walt's product and pay Mike his $5 million share, while Walt keeps the methylamine and keeps cooking. Jesse still wants out, so Walt takes on Todd as his new lab assistant and refuses to pay Jesse his cut, trying to manipulate him into staying; Jesse walks away anyway. Blocked from tailing Mike, the DEA turns to Mike's lawyer, Dan Wachsberger, who has been delivering hush money to Mike's men in prison. Dan cracks under pressure, and police close in on Mike while he is at a park with his granddaughter, forcing him to slip away and leave her behind. Walt brings Mike his escape bag of money and demands the names of the imprisoned men; Mike refuses and angrily tells Walt that his pride ruined everything they had with Gus. Enraged, Walt shoots him. Walt immediately realizes he could have gotten the names from Lydia, and Mike dies quietly beside a river at sunset.

episodes.title: Gliding Over All
episodes.summary: Walt has Todd help him dispose of Mike's body and car. Walt meets Lydia to get the names of Mike's nine imprisoned men; she proposes expanding their business to the Czech Republic, where she can distribute Walt's meth. Walt takes the names to Todd's uncle, Jack Welker, who leads a white supremacist gang with connections inside the prisons. In one coordinated wave, all nine men and Mike's lawyer are murdered within about two minutes. Walt's operation runs profitably for months, with Todd assisting in the lab. Skyler shows Walt a storage unit piled with more cash than they could ever spend or launder and asks how much is enough; soon after, Walt tells her he is out. He visits Jesse to deliver his share of the money in two bags, and they reminisce about their days cooking in the RV. The children move back home. At a family barbecue, Hank, using the Whites' bathroom, picks up Walt's copy of Leaves of Grass, sees Gale's handwritten inscription to 'W.W.', and realizes Walt is Heisenberg.

episodes.title: Blood Money
episodes.summary: A flash-forward shows Walt, now with hair and a beard, returning to his abandoned, fenced-off house, which has been vandalized and spray-painted with the word Heisenberg; he retrieves the ricin vial hidden behind an outlet, and a neighbor drops her groceries in shock at the sight of him. In the present, Hank leaves the barbecue and has a panic attack while driving home. He quietly pulls the Fring case files and confirms the handwriting in Walt's book matches Gale's. Haunted by the deaths of Mike and the boy from the train heist, Jesse asks Saul to deliver his money to Mike's granddaughter and the boy's family; Saul tells Walt instead, and Walt visits Jesse to insist, falsely, that Mike is alive. Unable to give the money away, Jesse flings stacks of cash out his car window while driving through a neighborhood. Lydia comes to the car wash begging Walt to return because the meth quality has dropped, but Skyler orders her never to come back. Walt's cancer has returned, and he is undergoing chemotherapy without telling his family. Discovering his book missing and a GPS tracker on his car, Walt confronts Hank in Hank's garage. Hank punches him and accuses him of being Heisenberg; Walt tells Hank his cancer is back and he will likely be dead within months, and warns him to tread carefully.

episodes.title: Buried
episodes.summary: An old man finds Jesse spinning absently on a playground merry-go-round after his cash-throwing spree, and the police pick Jesse up. Walt hides his fortune in seven barrels buried in the desert on the To'hajiilee Indian reservation and writes the GPS coordinates on a lottery ticket. Hank reaches Skyler first, at a diner, assuming she is Walt's victim and hoping she'll help build a case, but she refuses to talk without a lawyer and leaves. When Marie visits, Skyler can only say she's sorry; realizing Skyler knew about Walt's crimes before Hank was shot, Marie slaps her and tries to take baby Holly, then tells Hank he has to bring Walt down. Exhausted, Walt collapses at home and offers to turn himself in if Skyler keeps the money for the children, but she tells him to stay quiet because Hank has no real evidence. Lydia, needing better meth for her Czech buyers, tries to get Declan to use Todd as his cook; when Declan refuses, Jack's gang kills Declan and his crew and takes their lab equipment. Hank returns to the DEA office to find Jesse in custody.

episodes.title: Confessions
episodes.summary: The episode opens with Todd bragging to his uncle Jack about the train heist. Saul gets Jesse released after he refuses to talk to Hank. Walt and Skyler meet Hank and Marie at a restaurant to negotiate; Walt warns that the investigation will tear the family apart, and Skyler insists Walt is out of the business, but Hank refuses to back off. As they leave, Walt hands them a DVD: a fake confession in which Walt claims Hank was the real mastermind of the meth operation and forced Walt to cook for him. Hank then learns Marie accepted Walt's drug money to pay for his physical therapy, which makes Walt's story look believable and wrecks Hank's credibility. In the desert, Walt urges Jesse to take a new identity and leave town; Jesse begs Walt to stop manipulating him, and Walt answers with a hug. Jesse agrees to go, but while waiting for his ride, he realizes Saul's bodyguard Huell must have pickpocketed his ricin cigarette, meaning Walt poisoned Brock and manipulated him into turning on Gus. Enraged, Jesse beats the truth out of Saul, then breaks into the White house and douses it with gasoline.

episodes.title: Rabid Dog
episodes.summary: Walt arrives home to find Saul's car crashed in the driveway and the house soaked in gasoline, with no sign of Jesse. He explains the smell to his family with a story about a malfunctioning gas pump, moves them into a hotel, and leaves Jesse a voicemail asking to talk. When Skyler learns Jesse tried to burn the house down, she pushes Walt to have him killed. It turns out Hank followed Jesse and stopped him before he could set the fire; Hank brings Jesse home and records his full videotaped confession of everything he and Walt have done. With no physical evidence, Hank persuades Jesse to wear a wire and meet Walt in a crowded downtown plaza. At the last moment, Jesse spots a man he thinks is a hitman and backs out, then calls Walt and threatens to come after him where he really lives. Hank is furious, but Jesse says he has a better plan. Marie confides her rage at Walt to her therapist without revealing his crimes, and Walt calls Todd to arrange another job for his uncle's crew: killing Jesse.

episodes.title: To'hajiilee
episodes.summary: Walt asks Todd's uncle Jack to kill Jesse; Jack agrees on the condition that Walt cooks one more batch to teach Todd, and Walt reluctantly accepts. Hank and Gomez grab Saul's bodyguard Huell and, with a staged photo of Jesse apparently dead, scare him into revealing what he knows about Walt's money, including that it was moved in barrels. Saul tells Walt that Huell has vanished. Walt tries to lure Jesse out by having Andrea call him, but Hank intercepts the message. Hank stages a photo of a barrel of cash to make Walt believe Jesse has found the buried money. Panicking, Walt races to the To'hajiilee site while begging Jesse on the phone not to burn the cash, accidentally admitting to crimes as he talks. On the way, he calls Jack's crew for help. When he arrives and sees Jesse with Hank and Gomez, Walt calls Jack's men off and surrenders, and Hank handcuffs him and calls Marie to share the news. But Jack's gang shows up anyway, and a gunfight erupts between them and the two agents.

episodes.title: Ozymandias
episodes.summary: The shootout ends with Gomez dead and Hank wounded. Walt begs Jack to spare Hank, offering his entire buried fortune of about $80 million, but Hank refuses to plead for his life, and Jack shoots him dead. Jack's men dig up the barrels and take all but one, leaving Walt about $11 million. Walt points out where Jesse is hiding under a car, and before Jesse is dragged away, Walt cruelly tells him he watched Jane die and could have saved her. Todd takes Jesse prisoner, and after Jesse is beaten for information about what he told the DEA, he is chained in Todd's lab and forced to cook. Back in town, Marie tells Skyler that Hank has arrested Walt and makes her tell Walt Jr. the truth. When they get home, they find Walt frantically packing to flee; realizing Hank must be dead, Skyler grabs a knife and slashes Walt's hand. As they struggle, Walt Jr. protects his mother and calls 911, and Walt flees with baby Holly. That night, knowing the police are listening, Walt calls Skyler and berates her, taking all the blame himself to clear her. He leaves Holly at a fire station and contacts Saul's man who gives people new identities.

episodes.title: Granite State
episodes.summary: Ed, the man Saul uses to make people disappear, relocates Walt to a remote cabin in snowy New Hampshire, while Saul heads off to start a new life in Nebraska. Ed warns that leaving the cabin will likely get Walt caught. Jack's gang gets hold of Jesse's videotaped confession from Hank and Marie's house. After DEA questioning, Skyler is visited at home by Todd and masked men, who threaten her family if she ever mentions Lydia. Jesse nearly escapes from Jack's compound but is recaptured; as punishment, Todd takes him to Andrea's house and makes him watch as he shoots her dead. Months pass. Lonely and sick, Walt pays Ed $10,000 just to stay for an extra hour of company. Walt finally walks into town and calls Walt Jr. from a bar to arrange sending him money, but his son blames him for Hank's death, tells him he wishes he were dead, and hangs up. Walt calls the DEA to give himself up, but then sees Elliott and Gretchen on Charlie Rose minimizing his role in founding Gray Matter. When police surround the bar, Walt is already gone.

episodes.title: Felina
episodes.summary: Walt drives back to New Mexico. He sneaks into Elliott and Gretchen's home and gives them roughly $9.7 million in cash to put in a trust for Walt Jr. when he turns 18, warning that hired hitmen will kill them if they fail; the 'hitmen' are actually Badger and Skinny Pete aiming laser pointers. From the pair, Walt learns blue meth is still on the streets, meaning Jesse is alive and cooking. Walt slips ricin into Lydia's Stevia packet during her regular café meeting with Todd. He visits Skyler one last time, gives her a lottery ticket with the coordinates of Hank and Gomez's graves to use in a plea deal, and admits he did it all for himself because he liked it and was good at it. He watches Holly sleep and sees Walt Jr. from a distance. At Jack's compound, Walt tackles Jesse to the floor and triggers a remote-controlled M60 machine gun hidden in his car, killing Jack's gang. Jesse strangles Todd with his chains, and Walt shoots Jack. Walt, hit by his own gunfire, asks Jesse to kill him, but Jesse refuses and drives away free in Todd's car. Walt answers Lydia's call on Todd's phone to tell her she has been poisoned, then wanders into the lab and dies as police arrive.
